selector_regression_after_registry_appen.attribution: the seven red rows in the rev-20 sweep measured this script, not the registry: it paired each key's first task_id with its first check_id, and six of those combinations are combinations no card ever dispatched, which the handlers refuse with their own "unknown task/check/case selector" (seen in the child report, e.g. invocation 360d8e50). Re-running them with RESEARCHOS_GO set changed nothing, so the VB-2 environment hypothesis was wrong for these rows and is retracted. The v2 sweep below replays only selector triples taken from the plan's verification_commands for cards already ACCEPTED, which is the set whose resolution must not move when a key is appended.

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the first record test failed with NOT_FOUND: artifact unavailable: the helper sealed each artifact inside a transaction it then rolled back, so no cited artifact ever existed and the negative test that expects a refusal passed for the wrong reason
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the helper commits and reads the artifact back from domain_objects before returning
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: 0 (the input changed with the fix; a defect found by exercising the entry)

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the product section of the check was refused in three stages: 403 role not authorized for sealArtifact, then 428 If-Match required, then 412 STALE_REVISION
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the harness carries the contract's x-required-roles (OWNER+EXECUTOR) and re-reads ProjectState, the op's x-precondition-target, before each seal; the OWNER-only refusal is asserted as W0801-PRODUCT-SEAL-REFUSES-OWNER-ONLY so a PASS cannot come from bypassing the role table

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: an httptest loopback dial failed with a Windows connectex timeout while HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY were present in this shell
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the handler is driven in-process via httptest.NewRequest/Recorder, so the check does not depend on a proxy answering; a bound dispatcher command strips proxy variables anyway

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: adding the no-skip gate invalidated one of this card's own committed assertions: TestW0801RecordReuseDecisionSealsAndPromotes required the projection to agree with a stored promotion that had no RESEARCH row behind it
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the test now writes the research row through the product's own stage writer and asserts the agreement on those two rows, and a second test asserts the opposite direction: with no research row the reader must refuse. Both are recorded rather than the old assertion being quietly edited out
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: 0 (assertion changed together with the rule it tests)

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: five tests in the unbound legacy go test ./internal/domain suite were red while this card was in flight: this card's own record test plus TestW17UpgradeActiveRecovery, TestIntentQualifiedNativePlannerToBusinessDAG, TestRuntimeCoordinatorPurposeRevocation and TestRuntimeCoordinatorPeriodicHeartbeat

mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: recorded as measured, not retried to green

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the first mutation pass left four mutants that did not prove anything: M04-undeclared-field-ignored crashed (deleting the condition left the variable unused, so the package would not compile - a broken mutant, not a surviving one), and M12 cited-artifact-existence, M13 project-binding and M15 routing-guard survived because their assertions only asked whether an error came back, and a downstream step produced one anyway
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: M04 rewritten as reachable code (known initialised true). M12 given a distinguishing control: the artifact count must be unchanged by the refused call, which only the existence read can guarantee. M13 re-tested so every cited artifact really exists in the caller's project while the payload names a different project, which only the binding check can refuse. M15 re-tested by re-running the program itself under a foreign binding, so the refusal must come from the guard. Each is now named in the roster: W0801-RECORD-ABSENT-ARTIFACT-CREATES-NOTHING, W0801-RECORD-PROJECT-MISMATCH-REFUSED (message-bound), W0801-ROUTING-SELF-PROBE-REFUSES-FOREIGN-BINDING
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: one matrix re-run on the strengthened assertions

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the replacement assertion for M15 was itself wrong twice before it was right. First the matrix expected W0801-ROUTING-TRUTH-TABLE to go red, which cannot happen because the parent is always invoked under the correct binding. Then it expected the self-probe to go red, and on the next pass the probe passed for the wrong reason: with the guard deleted the child recursed until its report was unparsable, and the condition accepted any assertion count of one or below, including the sentinel for no parsable report at all
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: measured what the guard actually emits (status FAIL, zero assertion ids, the routing check alone in the failures list) and required exactly that shape, plus a 120s context timeout so a runaway child cannot hang the matrix. An empty roster and a full roster now mean different things
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: two further matrix passes after each probe defect

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the routing self-probe could nest without limit. Pass G ran M15 on this tree and the guard-less build re-ran the whole suite in a child that spawned its own child: several hundred copies of the check binary were alive on this host at once until the 120s context timeout cut them off. The assertion still went red, so no measurement was wrong, but the run put the machine under load and any later pass - including a reviewer building their own routing mutant - would repeat it
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the probe now marks its child (W0801_PROBE_CHILD=1) and a marked program reports the probe as failed at depth 1 instead of nesting further. The clean run never reaches the mark, so the reported tree is unchanged: three bound runs before and after the cap share one stdout digest, and pass H re-measured all 17 mutants at 17 caught with no process storm
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: 0 (the artifact changed with the fix; pass H is a new input, not a retry of pass G)

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the host suspended in the middle of delivery. The 17-mutant matrix (pass H) and the accepted-selector sweep were measured at 1611f274 with this card's changes present in the working tree, and the commit that records those changes, 2227afd6, landed after them. A re-run of the sweep at the committed HEAD was started and made no progress across the suspend, so it was stopped rather than left as a half-measured artifact
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the two trees are shown to be the same measurement instead of assumed to be: the bound command produced stdout.txt byte-identical at 1611f274 (e7cb21df, 95e6e379, 2420e149) and at 2227afd6 (c02b45ff), sha256 98820a8d96d9818f..., and every sweep row carries its own invocation id so a reader can re-run any single row at the committed tree
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: 0 (environment, not a retry of a failed input)

mid_card_failure_disclosed.what: the matrix script wrote its artifact only after deleting the scratch binary, so when Windows refused the delete (the probe child had just exited and still held the file) the run lost its JSON record - pass E measured 15 of 15 caught and left only a console log
mid_card_failure_disclosed.fix: the artifact is now written before any cleanup and cleanup failure is tolerated and reported. Pass E's log is frozen as mutation_matrix_log_attempt_e.txt and the matrix re-runs as pass F on the same final tree so the structured record exists
mid_card_failure_disclosed.retry_count: one matrix re-run caused by tooling, not by the code under test
